Exp. 1_behaviours

Gabriel Melhado

2026-07-17

Load the packages used for data manipulation, project-relative file paths, generalised linear mixed-effects models, residual diagnostics, estimated marginal means, plotting, and figure assembly. Using pacman::p_load() also installs packages that are not already available in the R library.

# Load packages
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, glmmTMB, DHARMa, performance, broom.mixed, car, dplyr, emmeans, ggeffects, scales, patchwork)
# Load Data
data <- read.csv(here("data", "exp1_data.csv"))
# Factorise IDs + treatment
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = factor(Treatment),
    Tank_ID   = factor(Tank_ID),
    Fish_ID   = factor(Fish_ID),
    Batch     = factor(Batch),
    Trial     = factor(Trial),
    Arena     = factor(Arena)
  )

Identify fish that did not emerge

Create a subset that excludes fish recorded as not emerging from the shelter, and compare the full and reduced sample sizes. This documents how many fish produced post-emergence behavioural observations and could be used in analyses that require emergence.

# Create a subset excluding fish not came out
# Remove fish that did not come out of shelter
data_subset <- subset(data, notes != "not came out")

# Check sample size
nrow(data)        # 160
## [1] 160
nrow(data_subset) # 126
## [1] 126

Analyse emergence probability

Convert the emergence outcome into a binary variable, where fish that did not emerge are coded as 0 and all others as 1. Fit a binomial generalised linear mixed-effects model to test whether emergence probability differs among treatments while controlling for body mass and accounting for tank-level clustering. Estimated marginal means are then returned on the probability scale.

data$emerged <- ifelse(data$notes == "not came out", 0, 1)

emergence_probability_model <- glmmTMB(emerged ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1|Tank_ID),
        family = binomial,
        data = data)


summary(emergence_probability_model)
##  Family: binomial  ( logit )
## Formula:          emerged ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##    172.9    188.3    -81.4    162.9      155 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID (Intercept) 0.08731  0.2955  
## Number of obs: 160, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Conditional model:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
## (Intercept)    2.145493   0.694110   3.091  0.00199 **
## TreatmentHigh  0.008245   0.494977   0.017  0.98671   
## TreatmentLow   0.229594   0.511853   0.449  0.65375   
## Body_mass     -1.413614   0.928424  -1.523  0.12786   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
Anova(emergence_probability_model)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: emerged
##            Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## Treatment 0.2543  2     0.8806
## Body_mass 2.3183  1     0.1279
emm <- emmeans(emergence_probability_model, ~ Treatment)

summary(emm, type = "response")
##  Treatment  prob     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  Control   0.783 0.0607 Inf     0.642     0.879
##  High      0.784 0.0616 Inf     0.640     0.881
##  Low       0.819 0.0579 Inf     0.678     0.907
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the logit scale

summary(data$Distance_moved)

summary(data$Time_shelter)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.

hist(data$Distance_moved)

hist(data$Time_not_moving)

hist(data$Time_shelter)

Model distance moved

Fit a Tweedie generalised linear mixed-effects model for distance moved. Treatment and body mass are included as fixed effects, tank is included as a random intercept, and DHARMa simulation-based diagnostics are used to assess residual behaviour, dispersion, zero inflation, and outliers before testing the overall treatment effect.

#Distance_moved
#Family tweedie
m2_distance_moved <- glmmTMB(Distance_moved ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID),
  data = data,
  family = tweedie(link = "log"))

summary(m2_distance_moved)
##  Family: tweedie  ( log )
## Formula:          Distance_moved ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1954.3   1975.8   -970.1   1940.3      153 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID (Intercept) 0.04904  0.2214  
## Number of obs: 160, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Dispersion parameter for tweedie family (): 14.8 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)    6.37803    0.39112  16.307   <2e-16 ***
## TreatmentHigh -0.35461    0.28670  -1.237    0.216    
## TreatmentLow  -0.02045    0.27741  -0.074    0.941    
## Body_mass     -0.71633    0.55420  -1.293    0.196    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Diagnosis
res_m2_distance_moved <- simulateResiduals(m2_distance_moved)
plot(res_m2_distance_moved)

testDispersion(res_m2_distance_moved)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0541, p-value = 0.648
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(res_m2_distance_moved)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = 0.983, p-value = 0.976
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_m2_distance_moved)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_m2_distance_moved
## outliers at both margin(s) = 2, observations = 160, p-value = 0.3647
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.001517409 0.044423034
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                                 0.0125
Anova(m2_distance_moved)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: Distance_moved
##            Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## Treatment 1.8804  2     0.3906
## Body_mass 1.6707  1     0.1962

Plot distance moved

# Plotting Distance_moved

# 1) Ensure treatment order
data$Treatment <- factor(
  data$Treatment,
  levels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
)

# 2) Fit Tweedie model
m2_distance_moved <- glmmTMB(
  Distance_moved ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID),
  data = data,
  family = tweedie(link = "log")
)

summary(m2_distance_moved)
##  Family: tweedie  ( log )
## Formula:          Distance_moved ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1954.3   1975.8   -970.1   1940.3      153 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID (Intercept) 0.04904  0.2214  
## Number of obs: 160, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Dispersion parameter for tweedie family (): 14.8 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)    6.37803    0.39112  16.307   <2e-16 ***
## TreatmentLow  -0.02045    0.27741  -0.074    0.941    
## TreatmentHigh -0.35461    0.28670  -1.237    0.216    
## Body_mass     -0.71633    0.55420  -1.293    0.196    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# 3) Get marginal means on the response scale
emm_dist_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(m2_distance_moved, ~ Treatment, type = "response")
)

print(emm_dist_df)
##  Treatment response       SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  Control   380.1215 75.25857 Inf  257.8676  560.3354
##  Low       372.4286 75.33911 Inf  250.5257  553.6481
##  High      266.6361 58.06943 Inf  173.9962  408.5998
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale
# 4) Standardise column names
cn <- names(emm_dist_df)

mean_col  <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])
lower_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)])
upper_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)])

if (is.na(mean_col) || is.na(lower_col) || is.na(upper_col)) {
  stop("Could not identify mean/CI columns in emmeans output. Run names(emm_dist_df).")
}

emm_dist_df <- emm_dist_df %>%
  mutate(Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "Low", "High"))) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

# 5) Palettes
pastel_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#A8D5BA",
  "Low"     = "#F9E79F",
  "High"    = "#F5B7B1"
)

dark_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#2E8B57",
  "Low"     = "#C9A227",
  "High"    = "#B22222"
)

# 6) Plot on original distance scale
p_distance <- ggplot() +
  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Distance_moved, fill = Treatment),
    alpha = 0.20,
    colour = NA,
    trim = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Distance_moved, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.60,
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_dist_df,
    aes(x = Treatment, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = emm_dist_df,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = mean, fill = Treatment),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dark_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 3000, by = 500),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 3000)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Distance moved (cm)"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p_distance)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "distance_travelled.pdf"),
  plot = p_distance,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "distance_travelled.jpg"),
  plot = p_distance,
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600
)

Model Shelter Use

Restrict the shelter-time analysis to observations strictly between zero and the 1,200-second trial limit, convert time to a proportion, and fit a beta mixed-effects model. The model tests treatment effects while controlling for body mass and tank, followed by DHARMa diagnostics and an omnibus treatment test.

#Time_shelter

data_moved <- subset(data, Time_shelter > 0 & Time_shelter < 1200)
data_moved$prop_shelter <- data_moved$Time_shelter / 1200

beta <-glmmTMB(
  prop_shelter ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID),
  family = beta_family(link="logit"),
  data = data_moved
)

summary(beta)
##  Family: beta  ( logit )
## Formula:          prop_shelter ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data_moved
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##    -73.3    -56.6     42.7    -85.3      114 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID (Intercept) 0.08021  0.2832  
## Number of obs: 120, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Dispersion parameter for beta family (): 1.63 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
## (Intercept)     0.7603     0.3924   1.938   0.0527 .
## TreatmentLow   -0.1154     0.2946  -0.392   0.6952  
## TreatmentHigh   0.3015     0.2985   1.010   0.3124  
## Body_mass      -0.1157     0.5560  -0.208   0.8352  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
res_beta <- simulateResiduals(beta)
plot(res_beta)

testDispersion(res_beta)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.96747, p-value = 0.712
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(res_beta)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = NaN, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_beta)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_beta
## outliers at both margin(s) = 1, observations = 120, p-value = 0.6171
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.0002109595 0.0455555132
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                            0.008333333
Anova(beta)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: prop_shelter
##            Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## Treatment 2.1087  2     0.3484
## Body_mass 0.0433  1     0.8352

Plot Shelter Use

# Plotting Time_shelter

# 1) Ensure treatment order
data$Treatment <- factor(
  data$Treatment,
  levels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
)

# 2) Create log-transformed shelter time
# log1p handles zeros safely
data$logTS <- log1p(data$Time_shelter)

# 3) Fit model
m_logTS <- glmmTMB(
  logTS ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = data
)

summary(m_logTS)
##  Family: gaussian  ( identity )
## Formula:          logTS ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##    617.1    635.6   -302.6    605.1      154 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID  (Intercept) 0.09699  0.3114  
##  Residual             2.48286  1.5757  
## Number of obs: 160, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for gaussian family (sigma^2): 2.48 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)     5.5835     0.4528  12.332   <2e-16 ***
## TreatmentLow   -0.1198     0.3424  -0.350   0.7265    
## TreatmentHigh   0.1487     0.3426   0.434   0.6642    
## Body_mass       1.2272     0.6388   1.921   0.0547 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# 4) Get marginal means on the LOG scale
emm_logTS_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans(m_logTS, ~ Treatment))

# 5) Back-transform to original time scale
cn <- names(emm_logTS_df)

mean_col  <- if ("emmean" %in% cn) "emmean" else stop("Can't find emmean column")
lower_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)])
upper_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)])

emm_logTS_df <- emm_logTS_df %>%
  mutate(Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "Low", "High"))) %>%
  rename(mean_log = !!mean_col, lower_log = !!lower_col, upper_log = !!upper_col) %>%
  mutate(
    mean  = exp(mean_log) - 1,
    lower = exp(lower_log) - 1,
    upper = exp(upper_log) - 1
  )

# 6) Palettes
pastel_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#A8D5BA",
  "Low"     = "#F9E79F",
  "High"    = "#F5B7B1"
)

dark_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#2E8B57",
  "Low"     = "#C9A227",
  "High"    = "#B22222"
)

# 7) Plot on original scale
p_shelter <- ggplot() +
  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Time_shelter, fill = Treatment),
    alpha = 0.20, colour = NA, trim = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Time_shelter, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.18, alpha = 0.55, size = 2
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_logTS_df,
    aes(x = Treatment, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.25, linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = emm_logTS_df,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = mean, fill = Treatment),
    shape = 21, size = 5, stroke = 1.2, colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dark_cols) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Time spent in shelter"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "shelter.pdf"),
  plot = p_shelter,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "shelter.jpg"),
  plot = p_shelter,
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600
)

Model freezing time

Fit a Tweedie generalised linear mixed-effects model for time spent not moving, used here as the measure of freezing behaviour. Treatment and body mass are included as fixed effects and tank as a random intercept. Simulation-based residual checks are performed before evaluating the overall treatment effect.

## Time_freezing
# Family: Tweedie
m1_time_not_moving <- glmmTMB(Time_not_moving ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID),
  data = data,
  family = tweedie(link = "log"))

summary(m1_time_not_moving)
##  Family: tweedie  ( log )
## Formula:          Time_not_moving ~ Treatment + Body_mass + (1 | Tank_ID)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1872.5   1894.0   -929.2   1858.5      153 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Tank_ID (Intercept) 0.08849  0.2975  
## Number of obs: 160, groups:  Tank_ID, 24
## 
## Dispersion parameter for tweedie family (): 12.6 
## 
## Conditional model:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)     5.8661     0.3916  14.979   <2e-16 ***
## TreatmentLow    0.2252     0.2991   0.753    0.452    
## TreatmentHigh  -0.1634     0.3074  -0.532    0.595    
## Body_mass      -0.6305     0.5484  -1.150    0.250    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Diagnosis
res_m1_time_not_moving <- simulateResiduals(m1_time_not_moving)
plot(res_m1_time_not_moving)

testDispersion(res_m1_time_not_moving)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.86705, p-value = 0.68
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(res_m1_time_not_moving)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = 1.0041, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_m1_time_not_moving)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_m1_time_not_moving
## outliers at both margin(s) = 0, observations = 160, p-value = 0.6427
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00000000 0.02279175
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                                      0
# Anova of the model
Anova(m1_time_not_moving)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: Time_not_moving
##            Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## Treatment 1.6556  2     0.4370
## Body_mass 1.3218  1     0.2503

## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale
# 4) Standardise column names
cn <- names(emm_freezing)

mean_col  <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])
lower_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)])
upper_col <- dplyr::first(cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)])

if (is.na(mean_col) || is.na(lower_col) || is.na(upper_col)) {
  stop("Could not identify mean/CI columns in emmeans output. Run names(emm_freezing).")
}

emm_freezing <- emm_freezing %>%
  mutate(Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "Low", "High"))) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

# 5) Colour palettes
pastel_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#A8D5BA",
  "Low"     = "#F9E79F",
  "High"    = "#F5B7B1"
)

dark_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#2E8B57",
  "Low"     = "#C9A227",
  "High"    = "#B22222"
)

# 6) Plot
p_freezing <- ggplot() +
  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Time_not_moving, fill = Treatment),
    alpha = 0.20,
    colour = NA,
    trim = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = data,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = Time_not_moving, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.18,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_freezing,
    aes(x = Treatment, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, colour = Treatment),
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = emm_freezing,
    aes(x = Treatment, y = mean, fill = Treatment),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dark_cols) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Time freezing"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p_freezing)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "Freezing.pdf"),
  plot = p_freezing,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "Freezing.jpg"),
  plot = p_freezing,
  width = 6,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600
)
#Figure 1
# Remove repeated x-axis titles from individual plots
p_distance_clean <- p_distance +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Distance moved (cm)") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

p_freezing_clean <- p_freezing +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Time freezing (s)") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

p_shelter_clean <- p_shelter +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Time spent in shelter (s)") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# Combine plots
figure_behaviour <- (
  p_distance_clean + p_freezing_clean + p_shelter_clean
) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A",
    caption = "Fluoxetine treatment"
  ) &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

figure_behaviour

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "behaviour_figure.pdf"),
  plot = figure_behaviour,
  width = 12,
  height = 4.5
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "behaviour_figure.jpg"),
  plot = figure_behaviour,
  width = 12,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 600
)
